question: Article 7 of Directive 2009/147/EC recognises hunting as a legitimate activity, and Article 2 requires economic and recreational requirements to be taken into account.

Traditional hunting is geared towards the conservation of species, but many EU rules increase costs and red tape: the ban on lead shot, which will make new ammunition and, probably, new weapons obligatory; the periodic checks introduced in 2017 without an impact assessment (now in Directive (EU) 2021/555) and which increase the number of certificates and requirements for citizens who have already been verified; the health requirements concerning live decoys and avian influenza; the sourcing of decoys almost exclusively from breeders; and disproportionate reporting requirements for regions and hunters, arising from Articles 9(3) and 12 of Directive 2009/147/EC.

None of these measures has been assessed based on its cumulative effect, resulting in a fragmented, costly and bureaucratic picture, which risks reducing the number of hunters and encouraging poaching. In view of the above: 1.
Has the Commission assessed the cumulative impact these rules have on traditional hunting, in the light of Article 2 of Directive 2009/147/EC and the principle of proportionality?
Will it propose a simplification omnibus that reduces fragmentation, costs and red tape in this area, including reporting?
How does it intend to prevent the increase in costs and red tape from encouraging poaching?
